text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — we flipped the hot-prefix primer on the canary pools for raptor-7b a few hours ago and got some solid wins.
DevBot: canary deploy succeeded (logs: https://deploys.internal/rw/1745411200) :white_check_mark:
Kevin: numbers?
Maya: short summary: p50 latency down ~9.8% across the sampled chat workload, p95 down ~6%, and measured token CPU/GPU cost reduction ~18% on the canary hosts. Throughput stayed flat.
Jordan: nice. any cold-start impact?
Maya: small cold-start mem bump (~+120MB/process) and a +1–2ms start latency for totally unseen prefixes. TTL evictions clear most of it, so steady-state memory is fine. Tail for rare prefixes slightly higher but overall tail improved on typical traffic.
Anita: did long-context tests regress (8k+)?
Maya: long-context benchmarks are neutral — no sign of regression in our 8k/16k test sets. I ran the microbench harness across seq lengths.
Maya: benchmark command we ran:
```
./run_bench --model raptor-7b --workload chat-24k --iters 1000 --save ./results/hotprefix-canary.json
```
Kevin: roll to prod plan? staged?
Maya: proposing staged rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with checkpoints at each step (p50/p95, evict-rate, oom-events). If any regression >3% p95 or unexpected OOMs, rollback. I'll open the rollout ticket now.
Infra-Bot: created rollout ticket RW-3129 (assignee: Maya)
DevBot: suggested metrics to watch: token-throughput, prefix-evict-rate, p50, p95, GPU-util, per-host mem-usage. Alerts: p95 increase >3% or evict-rate spike >2x.
Jordan: ack — will keep an eye on dashboards and run a quick A/B against the control pool for the next 24h. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks all. Posting full canary artifacts and raw bench results in the ticket. Will follow up with a short postmortem if anything odd shows up.
